          Differential navigator

          Start from what you see

          Pick the finding in front of you. Each differential has a stepwise approach, the discriminating features, a live example of every option and a drill. Built from Section V of your emergency ECG textbook (Hudson et al., 2023), in Sinus's own words.

          Caliper drill

          Measure it

          0/0within tolerance

          Drag the two orange calipers onto the waveform. Tap the strip to move the nearest caliper. One small square is 40 ms; one big square is 200 ms.

          ECG lab

          Build your own tracing

          Change one variable at a time and watch what happens across all twelve leads. The readout measures lead II the way you would with calipers.

            Free resources

            Move on to real tracings

            Tracings in Sinus are drawn by a teaching model: clean, idealised and generated fresh each time. Real ECGs are noisier and messier, so pair every module here with real cases from these free libraries. They open on their own sites.

            Real ECG library

            Real patients, open databases

            More free libraries

            A study loop that works

            1. Study one module in Learn, with the findings overlay off first, then on.
            2. Score 8 out of 10 in Quiz on that module.
            3. Open ECG Wave-Maven, pick random case mode so the diagnosis stays hidden, and write your full read before revealing the answer.
            4. Look up anything you missed in the LITFL ECG Library and note the one feature that would have changed your read.
            5. Revisit weak patterns: the quiz automatically shows you the ones you miss more often.
            Reading room · real ECGs

            Read real ECGs until it is second nature

            One real recording after another, labels hidden. The ones you miss come back; new ones come first.
